claims.claim: Reviewers report that the multiplayer system is overly restrictive, requiring each player to view cutscenes independently or solo before others can join.

citations.review_text:
The game could be fun -- with friends. Too bad I'm barely able to play it in such a manner since each individial player must seek out the objective on visually loaded maps and watch the cutscene on their own, only after which the co-op is possible. The counter-intuitive UI and controls do not help with that, as well as inability to re-bind the keys on a controller makes for a very clunky and frustrating experience. 

All the NPCs have archetypes but no personalities, which is boring. 

The character designs and animations are nice... if you're into anime. Well, I'm not.

This game's main draw is co-op.
This game refuses to let you play co-op at almost every turn, with hundreds of tiny little restrictions to the point that you basically can only play co-op after you've already played the entire game solo.

I hate everything about the design decisions made to make a co-op game that essentially locks you out of co-op.

Writing this under the context that I'm going to continue playing this game, mostly because it's a gift from my partner so that we could play together.

I cannot recommend this game to people.

Going over the good first, the player controls actually quite well. It's responsive, what you input is what you see happening, the worlds and art design are quite beautiful in this game and the base itself is fun to traverse through having multiple levels to it. I did also quite like the intro as well. That being said, there's so much about this game that's utter crap.

First of all, for a game that forces you into online multiplayer, it is prolific in the amount of effort going into specifically blocking you from being able to actually play multiplayer at every single stage. No, you're not allowed to "join a player on a quest or expedition", why would you ever want to do that? You have to go and play solo up until you reach a cutscene, and THEN either fire an SOS, extract from the mission and start it again, or if you're lucky enough, tell them that you're available to be joined and wait for them to ready, join, and reach your location (that is of the game even lets other players join you). This is all ontop of not even being able to see your players in the very clearly multiplayer designed base, nor being able to even see who's in your party unless you open up a specific part of your menu. And I WISH that was everything about the MP.

Going out on an expedition to "investigate" a new monster is pointless tedium. The clues you need to investigate within the maps have zero logic or consistency to them and are placed wherever the hell the developers wanted to put them, so you're spent running around for 30 minutes just hoping you come across a segment of a track that maybe possibly does... something? You also have to hit a seemingly four foot trigger box placed in one singular particular spot in the entirety of a given map to watch the cutscene and progress the mission and if …

The most unintuitive POS game I have ever played. I must be stupid because I spent every minute wondering where the hell to go and what to do. The interface is more cramped than Oliver Twist's grandparents and it is harder to join your friends than dark souls (apparently you have to join a mission, watch the cutscenes, leave and then try and join your friends again? And it's been a known issue since the game came out?) Also it straight up won't let you leave the game if you're in a mission, you've got to make it across the other side of the map and talk to an NPC just to be allowed to quit the game from within the menu. Ridiculous.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game reviewers mention unskippable cutscenes and multiplayer hurdles while noting performance demands on lower-end hardware.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that cutscenes during the campaign cannot be skipped.

citations.review_text:
It's a game. As much as Freedom Unite defined my childhood, 3rd Portable to distract me from studies on high school, MHGU/MHXX to be a cool game featuring an edgelord dragon and actual insect bosses alongside one that really loves wheels, World is just... boring. I keep checking out when cutscenes happen; wish they were skippable. X???'???? and S???? I??????? are boring "last bosses". Like, come on, let's think of the past generations "last bosses".
The story, like I said, I keep checking out. I even turned off the voice volume at some point just so I can read the story. I don't care at all at this point meeting Fatalis, Uninstalled the game. It may say "49 hours" but I've been playing offline and online.

The strength of this game however, is in its gameplay loop. If there was a mod or an update that just makes cutscenes skippable, I would take it. I enjoy the game playing every weapons (not ranged though).
But there's a really problem this game have: variants of past bosses. I honestly think having good graphics is what hurt this game. Having "so much graphics" meant I'll have to fight Rathian in 5 flavors, a variant of each monster that has a long-winded attack; I get it. Variants are OK because it gives ideas for the player that this boss has the same style of fighting. But, why though?
Because of graphics. If the game wasn't such a storage hog now and before, this game would have more bosses. Please show me the same large monster encounter screaming at my face or lunging at m-FAKE OUT, there's the boss variant! Predictable. Where's the giant crab? Where's Seltas? Where's the non-bird bosses? I know there's a Rajang, but come on, no dung-thrower monkey with a mushroom on it's back? World has no levity and creativity at all! Where's my emo dragon that turns other large monsters into emos, and then becomes Michael Jackson at the end? Where's the cool eastern dragon that makes you take a shower and soap with a slip and slide? WHERE'S THE COOL PRAYING MANTIS BE…
Great combat and really addicting play pattern. Not being able to skip some cutscenes was annoying though.

It is one of those games where you have to play 30 hours before you get to the good part.
And then you have to grind another 70 hours to unlock everything the game has to offer.
And even then you only unlocked it, you don't have it. You have grind another 20-50 hours to craft what you fancy and all the nice armors and weapons mods.

So it's a good game, rather technical, but the grind is too much for me to continue.
I gave it the fairest shot I could, but that's it for me.

I only powered though all this to play with a friend, but couldn't most of the time because of this game's insistance on not letting me go multiplayer for most of the storyline. This makes no sense.
That and unskipable cutscene (sorry but I'm not here for the forgetable story with cliché characters) is a real test of patience if you intend to play with friends.

If you're liiking for a forever game you kind endlessly grind until the end of time, then it's a good choice.

citations.review_text:
[h1][b] The good [/b][/h1]
The base game is very enjoyable, despite the flaws. The gameplay is fun, the monsters are interesting and it even has some sort of a story to it. The core gameplay loop is satisfying when it works properly.

The environments look really nice, are decently large and very dense.

Some of the fights are very cinematic and intense.

The soundtrack is very good.

[h1][b] The bad [/b][/h1]
The game is extremely clunky, fairly buggy, and decently grindy. You will miss half of your hits if you play a weapon that swings slowly because of the clunk.

Your weapon will hit where your character is pointing, not where you are looking. Takes some getting used to.

The game crashes somewhat often, and will sometimes kick you out of multiplayer.

Flying monsters will spend half of the time flying around pretending to be a plane, making it very frustrating to fight them with a melee weapon. Yes, I know they are supposed to fly, but at least let me fight them. Then, after flying around for about 5 minutes, they will leave the area, fly all the way across the map, and good luck finding them again. The tracking system decides at random whether it wants to track the monster or something completely random. 

Progression also requires fighting the exact same monster a few too many times for what is often a very mediocre upgrade. It gets pretty annoying when you have to fight the same thing for the 15th time.

As for Iceborne - I did not like it, and it even made me quit the game. The area is nice, but that's about it. Monsters have way too much health and take too long to kill. Most of it is just more of the same, only with the health and damage cranked up to 11. Contrary to popular opinion, I don't think the DLC is worth it, even though it adds a couple of cool monsters.

[h1][b] The abysmal [/b][/h1]
The multiplayer. You are forced to join a quest, watch the cutscenes, leave the quest and only then you may invite your friends through posting a quest (yes, every…
bad pc's will crash often if you don't turn down graphics but other than that its very good and hard

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features unskippable cutscenes and a focus on story elements such as following the Handler.

citations.review_text:
Monster Hunter: World was my entry to what is now possibly my favorite series. I had never played the series before or seen it, only heard about it through a buddy of mine. So I started this game basically entirely blind. Even now this game captures some joy in me that nothing else is quite able to.
I don't make promises often, but I can promise you that if you start playing this game you will be stepping into a wonderful world of nature backed up by weighty and satisfying combat. It is not perfect, it is at times clunky and too busy insisting on itself to give even a singular ♥♥♥♥ about the user. But if you jive with the series I don't think you'll find anything quite like it. 
As said before, the game is not perfect. Some flaws are vestigial from previous games and some are new. I think World is as equally deserving of my praises as it is my criticisms so

tl;dr the most prominent sin of this game is the AAA slop that is injected from the beginning. Though it started with MH4 this game continues to double down on giving extra attention to the story of the game. It is one thing to add some story behind the various NPCs and quests we do, unskippable cutscenes and a literal escort quest are another thing. I do not enjoy having to follow the dreaded Handler and listen to her talk about things I surely would have learned by exploring and playing a little bit on my own. I don't appreciate repeatedly having to sit through more of it as the game goes on. I don't mind the big talks with the whole crew back at base, what I object to is it getting directly in the way of my hunting. It's somehow worse in multiplayer because you can't even join the quest until the cutscene is over and if you haven't done it yourself the method is to get to the cutscene, watch it, leave your quest and then join your buddy's or vice versa. This aspect of the game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mind numbingly archaic and untested I am still amazed that this was pushed to production and then to consumers. But that…

This is my first Monster Hunter game, and I actually dropped it about 14 hours in, right before the Zorah Magdaros mission. 

The game did a poor job explaining weapon controls and movesets. Chasing and fighting monsters solo was a nightmare, even with the defender gear. Finding openings to attack was tough, and quest usually ended in a time-out or failed. On top of that, I hate the ancient forest map which is a total maze, and fighting and chasing Rathalos there as a noob without knowing the flashpod trick makes me want to quit this game forever. The real trash design is the unskippable cutscene, and they are incredibly long and boring. I don't know whose stupid idea it is.

After half a year, I picked the game back just to finish the main plot and not waste my money. One of my steam family member had the Iceborne DLC. Having access to the clutch claw, tenderizing, and flinch shots completely fixed the experience for me. 

I mained Long Sword to finish the base game. After entering the DLC, I tried all the weapons. My favorite three are Insect Glaive, Switch Axe, and Charge Blade. I like the creativity behind their moveset designs. Additionally, I really like the arena quests and challenges more because they remove the annoying tracking, chasing monster from one region to another, and let you focus straight on the fight.

Overall, this game ended up giving me a truly unique experience. Buying the DLC is an absolute must if you want to enjoy it. All the good content is definitely in the DLC.

Even though MH Wilds got released, you still have to try it out. 

Pros:
Addictive gameplay, adequate performance, vast range of possible interactions with the world and cool armor sets... To be honest it's all you need nowadays, because modern games are lacking even these major necessities.

Cons:
Handler.(Can be fixed with mods)
Mediocre story and unskipable cutscenes on different save slot (can be fixed with mods)
Sometimes bs hitboxes, but it's a problem for people who decided to hunt Alatreon and Fatalis ( side quests that are non essential for progression in story )

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Iceborne expansion and its features like the clutch claw significantly improve the gameplay experience.

citations.review_text: I cannot stress this enough. If you want to get into the newer Monster Hunter games, PLEASE start with this one. The weapon abilities are decently easy to master, the selection of monsters is immaculate, and the playstyle and story of the game just flow together so perfectly. 10/10 game, I've played since 2020 (on different platforms than steam), and could not recommend this game more. I suggest buying the pack of base game and the Iceborne DLC, mostly so you get the ability to use the clutch claw, which will help your hunts SO much.

800 hours in and my therapist says I need to talk about something other than monster weaknesses. She is wrong. MHW is a certified masterpiece and I will die on this hill, specifically while a Rajang throws me off it. Every single weapon is a different game. The world breathes, the monsters have more character than most RPG protagonists and the Iceborne expansion said hold my Astera Jerky and doubled everything. There is technically a story. Nobody knows what it is. Nobody cares. You are here to find a monster, learn its entire life story through its movement patterns and then turn it into a funny hat. This game grabbed an entire generation by the collar, said welcome to the hunt, and never let go. No notes whatsoever. Real ones know.
[b][9.5/10][/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the game requires a heavy time investment due to extensive grinding and RNG mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Great game and got it on sale. Played some previous entries of the franchise before this, got rise, still playing this, still great even years after its launch. Would recommend unless you hate learning and value time because it's grindy as hell (you will learn real love)

Bless you gamers

Fun to play, but absolutely miserable to 100%. Even though I mainly used the Meowcano glitch to kill monsters after defeating Shara Ishvalda and entering the Guiding Lands, the RNG in this game is still pure ball torture. And it’s not just RNG getting in your way, it’s also a bunch of game mechanics you barely notice during a casual playthrough. For example, the game forces you to leave an expedition and come back every 3 Paw Swap cycles, so you can’t grind it efficiently even if you have enough resources to do it all day. Combine that with RNG-based treasure tip drops and 60 total treasures, and congratulations - you’re stuck there forever.

Crown farming (even with investigation save-scumming and an overlay that shows whether a monster has a crown or not) was ridiculously inconsistent. Sometimes you get miniature and gold crowns from Nergigante back-to-back, and sometimes you spend 6 hours straight resetting for a stupid gold crown on Vaal Hazak. I’m honestly scared to imagine how people farm this garbage on consoles. I saw one guy on Reddit who farmed a gold crown for Vaal Hazak for an entire year and still didn’t get the crown he needed.

There are also a bunch of smaller issues:

1) The idiotic camera auto-focus on monsters after increasing Scoutfly level by picking up tracks, even if you’ve already encountered the monster before. That mechanic got me killed several times.
2) The inability to skip the time of day. You literally have to wait around 15 minutes, which is especially irritating when you’re trying to catch endemic life that only spawns during the day or night.
3) Another “fantastic” feature: you can’t skip the 60-second timer after killing a monster (which, as far as I know, you could do in previous games). During a normal playthrough you barely notice it, but when you’re farming elder dragons, which you can’t trap-spam (either for research levels or Master Rank), it intentionally slows down your progress.
4) The absolutely stupid Palico AI during ba…

This game and the whole series has meant a lot to me and i think anyone who's thinking of playing definitely should as it is a really fun experience that's surprises with how much it's held up and although the grind can be a bit maddening sometimes this game will always have a special place in my heart as well as its siblings rise and wilds and ever since i first dipped my toes in i could tell this series is a hard one to love for a lot a people specially the farther back you go but if your the right kinda crazy with some bright eyes who loves Monster Hunter like me then you'll love the hell outta the whole series.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game suffers from demanding graphical performance on budget hardware.

citations.review_text:
A visually and mechanically stunning game about hunting monsters but in a way that helps the environment instead of hindering it, Monster Hunter World will leave you pleasantly indecisive at the choice of weapons for your craft and wondering how hunting 40 of the same monster to get a good armor set isn't considered genocide. 

The story's not exactly phenomenal but it exists to justify the rest of the game and does its purpose, with a few minor standout characters. Environmentally the game feels like a living, breathing thing with entire open areas of flora and fauna going about their daily lives and even clashing with one another actively, and is easily the standout design focus of the game. No other game has felt as active around me as this one does, to this day. 

Just few minor gripes I have aside from the story, notably that graphically the game is quite demanding so players with budget PCs may not get as much out of this one than others. If you want to see the game through, you will also have to deal with certain fights that spike drastically in difficulty compared to 95% of pacing elsewhere, especially if you want to fight the last few optional monsters. But generally patience is a virtue, and many fights can be won through wars of attrition and careful planning. Maybe just prepare to reach gear cap by the last few fights and boost your hunter rank.

Kind of surprised that this game runs smoothly on my laptop, but it does. This game is one of the strongest entries in the MH franchise. The tracking system and the maps are absolutely fantastic. I'm not a fan of the increased focus on story or the clutch claw; however, I really like the way they did investigations in this game. Much better than guild quests in 4U or investigations in wilds. Highly recommend.

Even though MH Wilds got released, you still have to try it out. 

Pros:
Addictive gameplay, adequate performance, vast range of possible interactions with the world and cool armor sets... To be honest it's all you need nowadays, because modern games are lacking even these major necessities.

Cons:
Handler.(Can be fixed with mods)
Mediocre story and unskipable cutscenes on different save slot (can be fixed with mods)
Sometimes bs hitboxes, but it's a problem for people who decided to hunt Alatreon and Fatalis ( side quests that are non essential for progression in story )

I first heard of monster hunter in 2024, and it was that one game that I was always searching for but could never find. my first monster hunter was wilds which I'm sure are some people's first as well.  After a while I decided to try monster hunter world for the first time with some friends, and it was the most fun I have had in a while. I would say that it was a lot harder in monster hunter world for me then it was in wilds but in the end that's what made the game more fun for me(although Raging Brachy and Fatalis were pushing me to the verge of blowing my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brains out).
